intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an outdoor sunrise yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud, surrounded by lush jungle and rice paddies. Many local instructors offer small group classes here, blending breathwork and asana with the natural landscape. A deeply restorative and spiritual experience unique to Bali.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner-friendly surf lesson on the golden sands of Seminyak Beach, one of Bali's most beautiful and accessible surf spots. After your lesson, relax and watch the legendary Bali sunset with a fresh coconut in hand. Local surf schools offer affordable 2-hour sessions with boards and instructors included.

experiences.name: Nusa Penida Island Day Trip & Kelingking Beach
experiences.description: Take a fast boat from Sanur to the stunning island of Nusa Penida and visit the iconic Kelingking Beach, often called the T-Rex cliff viewpoint. Snorkel in crystal-clear waters at Crystal Bay and explore dramatic coastal cliffs. A full-day guided tour typically includes transport, snorkeling gear, and a local lunch.

experiences.name: Traditional Balinese Cooking Class & Market Tour
experiences.description: Start your morning at a local market in Ubud with a guide who explains traditional Balinese ingredients and spices. Then head to an open-air kitchen to prepare 5–6 authentic dishes including satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding. You'll eat everything you cook and take home a recipe booklet.

experiences.name: Multi-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Spend several sessions over your 13-day stay at The Yoga Barn, one of Bali's most celebrated wellness centers. Choose from daily drop-in classes in Hatha, Vinyasa, Yin, or meditation. The lush jungle setting, world-class instructors, and community atmosphere make this a bucket-list yoga destination. Drop-in classes are affordable and schedules are flexible.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Bali (Flight LH lands at 13:00) — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront. Freshen up, unpack, and take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings. Dip your toes in the warm Indian Ocean and enjoy the stunning coastal views right outside your door.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest local night market (pasar malam) on foot. Browse street food stalls, soak in the atmosphere, and pick up any essentials you may need for your stay.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a quick snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Warung (local Indonesian eatery) near the resort — try Nasi Goreng or Mie Goreng for under IDR 30,000 (~$2 USD)
meals.dinner: Local night market street food — satay skewers, tempeh, and fresh coconut water for under IDR 50,000 (~$3 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 13:00 arrival. Exchange some cash at the airport for better rates. Keep your first evening light to recover from travel. Warm summer weather expected — stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Start your first full day with a sunrise yoga session on the beach directly in front of the Aegean Bliss Resort. Many beachfront resorts offer complimentary or low-cost yoga at sunrise. Alternatively, find a free-to-join community yoga session on the sand (common in Bali's beach towns). Practice as the sun rises over the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest popular beach (Kuta, Seminyak, or Legian depending on resort location) for swimming and sunbathing. Rent a surfboard from a local beach shack for IDR 50,000–80,000/hour and take a beginner surf lesson — many local instructors offer affordable 1-hour lessons for IDR 150,000–200,000.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Bali sunset from the beach. Join other travelers and locals gathered along the shore. Grab a Bintang beer or fresh juice from a beachside warung and enjoy the golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit plate, banana pancakes, and tea/coffee at a local warung near the resort — IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.lunch: Beach warung lunch — Nasi Campur (mixed rice with sides) for IDR 35,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Budget beachside restaurant — grilled fish with steamed rice and vegetables for IDR 60,000–80,000

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen before beach activities. Warm weather around 25°C with low rain chance — perfect beach day. Bargain politely when renting surf equipment.

day_by_day.morning: Join an early morning yoga class at a local budget-friendly yoga studio near your resort. Many studios in Bali offer drop-in classes for IDR 80,000–150,000. Focus on a Hatha or Vinyasa flow class to energize your day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby Hindu temple — Pura Tanah Lot or a local sea temple depending on your location. Entrance fees are typically IDR 20,000–60,000. Explore the temple grounds, observe traditional offerings, and learn about Balinese Hindu culture. Sarongs are usually available to borrow at the entrance.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through a local arts and crafts market. Browse handmade batik fabrics, wooden carvings, and silver jewelry. Practice your bargaining skills — prices are always negotiable. Pick up small souvenirs without breaking the budget.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or avocado toast at a budget café near the yoga studio — IDR 40,000–60,000
meals.lunch: Warung near the temple — Lawar (traditional Balinese mixed vegetables and meat) with rice for IDR 30,000–45,000
meals.dinner: Local Padang-style restaurant — self-serve dishes priced by selection, budget IDR 50,000–70,000 for a filling meal

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for temple visits — cover shoulders and knees. A sarong and sash are required and often provided for free or a small donation. Temples are free or very low cost to enter.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or scooter (IDR 50,000–80,000/day for bicycle; IDR 70,000–100,000/day for scooter) and explore the surrounding neighborhood. Ride through rice paddies, local villages, and quiet back roads. Enjoy the fresh morning air before the heat of the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a quieter, less touristy beach nearby for a peaceful afternoon swim. Bali has many hidden beach gems away from the crowds. Bring a book, snorkel gear (rentable for IDR 30,000–50,000), and enjoy the crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak fire dance performance — one of Bali's most iconic cultural experiences. Performances are held at various temples (Pura Uluwatu is famous for this) and cost IDR 100,000–150,000. The sunset backdrop makes it unforgettable.

meals.breakfast: Nasi Jinggo — small rice parcels wrapped in banana leaf sold by street vendors for IDR 5,000–10,000 each. Have 3–4 for a full breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from a local minimart (Indomaret or Alfamart) — instant noodles, fresh fruit, and snacks for IDR 30,000–40,000
meals.dinner: Warung dinner near the Kecak performance venue — Babi Guling (suckling pig) or Ayam Betutu (slow-cooked chicken) for IDR 50,000–80,000

day_by_day.notes: If renting a scooter, ensure you have an international driving permit and always wear a helmet. Kecak performances are weather-dependent — check schedules in advance. Arrive early for good seating.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated yoga morning — attend a 2-hour morning yoga and meditation retreat at a local shala. Many budget yoga centers in Bali offer immersive morning sessions including pranayama (breathwork) and guided meditation for IDR 100,000–200,000. This is a core experience for yoga-focused travelers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local traditional market (Pasar Badung or nearest local market). Wander through stalls selling tropical fruits, spices, flowers for offerings, and local snacks. This is a fantastic cultural immersion experience and completely free to browse.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort beachfront. Watch the stars from the beach — Bali's low light pollution in beach areas makes for excellent stargazing. Bring a sarong to lie on the sand.

meals.breakfast: Post-yoga smoothie and granola at the yoga studio café — IDR 40,000–55,000
meals.lunch: Fresh tropical fruits and local snacks bought directly from the traditional market — IDR 20,000–30,000 for a colorful spread
meals.dinner: Cook or assemble a simple meal using market ingredients, or dine at the resort's most affordable menu option — budget IDR 60,000–90,000

day_by_day.notes: Visit the traditional market early (before 9am) for the freshest produce and most authentic atmosphere. Bring small denomination bills for market purchases. Yoga sessions fill up — book ahead if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ubud (approximately 1–1.5 hours from beach areas by shared shuttle — Perama or similar services cost IDR 50,000–80,000 one way). Visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary (IDR 80,000 entrance) — a lush jungle sanctuary with hundreds of macaque monkeys and ancient temples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud town on foot. Walk through the Ubud Art Market for handicrafts and textiles. Visit the Ubud Palace (Puri Saren Agung) — free to view from outside, small donation appreciated. Stroll the famous Campuhan Ridge Walk — a free 2km scenic trail through jungle and rice terraces.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by shared shuttle. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a traditional Balinese massage at a budget spa near the resort — a one-hour full body massage costs IDR 80,000–120,000.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort warung before departure — Bubur Ayam (chicken rice porridge) for IDR 25,000–35,000
meals.lunch: Ubud warung lunch — Bebek Goreng (fried duck) or vegetarian Gado-Gado (peanut sauce salad) for IDR 40,000–60,000
meals.dinner: Warung near the resort upon return — keep it simple with Mie Goreng and fresh juice for IDR 35,000–50,000

day_by_day.notes: Secure bags tightly in the Monkey Forest — monkeys are known to grab loose items. Book the shuttle in advance from the resort reception. Ubud is slightly cooler and greener than the coast — bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Beach yoga at sunrise — unroll your mat on the sand for a self-guided practice or join a free community beach yoga session. Focus on sun salutations facing the ocean. Follow with a refreshing morning swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby waterfall — Bali has stunning waterfalls accessible on a scooter or via organized budget tours (IDR 150,000–250,000 including transport). Popular options include Tegenungan Waterfall (IDR 20,000 entrance) which is relatively close to beach areas. Swim in the natural pool at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free or donation-based sunset meditation session on the beach. Many yoga teachers and wellness practitioners host these informal gatherings. Reflect on the week's experiences.

meals.breakfast: Jaja Bali (traditional Balinese snacks) and black rice pudding from a street vendor — IDR 20,000–30,000
meals.lunch: Picnic by the waterfall — grab provisions from a local warung before heading out. Budget IDR 30,000–40,000.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for the week's midpoint — a beachside seafood dinner with grilled prawns, fish, and rice for IDR 80,000–120,000

day_by_day.notes: Waterfall areas can be slippery — wear appropriate footwear. The 30mm monthly rainfall is low, but brief afternoon showers are possible — carry a small poncho. Midway through the trip — a great time to reflect and recharge.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget cooking class — many local families offer authentic Balinese cooking classes starting with a market visit for IDR 200,000–350,000. Learn to make Bumbu Bali (spice paste), Satay Lilit, and traditional desserts. A wonderful hands-on cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at the resort pool or beach after the morning activity. Read, journal, or simply enjoy the warm Bali sun. Take a slow afternoon swim and recharge your energy.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local beach strip after dark — many beach towns come alive at night with fire dancers, live music at warungs, and social gatherings. Enjoy the atmosphere without spending much.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the cooking class — banana and peanut butter toast at a café for IDR 25,000–35,000
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you cooked during the cooking class — included in the class price
meals.dinner: Warung on the beach strip — Nasi Goreng Seafood for IDR 45,000–65,000 with a cold Bintang beer (IDR 30,000–40,000)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class the day before to secure a spot. Most classes include a market tour, all ingredients, recipes to take home, and the meal. Great value for money and a lasting skill.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga flow at the resort or nearby studio — focus on restorative yoga or yin yoga for deep stretching and relaxation. Follow with a 20-minute meditation on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling trip — join a budget group snorkeling tour from the beach (IDR 150,000–250,000 including equipment and boat). Explore coral reefs and colorful marine life. Popular snorkeling spots include areas near Nusa Lembongan or local reef areas depending on your resort location.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free Balinese ceremony or temple festival if one is happening nearby — Bali has ceremonies almost daily. Ask your resort staff about local events. Observe respectfully from a distance.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit salad and coconut yogurt at a health café — IDR 35,000–50,000
meals.lunch: Post-snorkeling warung meal on the boat or at the beach — Ikan Bakar (grilled fish) with sambal and rice for IDR 50,000–70,000
meals.dinner: Local family warung — Soto Ayam (chicken soup) with rice cakes for IDR 30,000–45,000

day_by_day.notes: Apply waterproof reef-safe sunscreen before snorkeling. Snorkeling tours often depart early morning or mid-morning — confirm timing when booking. Bring an underwater camera or waterproof phone case for photos.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a lesser-known beach or hidden cove near your resort — ask locals for recommendations for beaches without crowds. Spend the morning swimming, reading, and enjoying the peaceful atmosphere. Collect shells or simply meditate by the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local village on foot or by bicycle. Visit a family compound, watch artisans at work (woodcarving, silver jewelry making, batik painting), and engage with the community. Many villages welcome curious visitors — always ask permission before photographing people.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails (or mocktails) at a budget beach bar — many offer happy hour deals. Watch the sun sink into the Indian Ocean with new friends made along the way.

meals.breakfast: Bubuh Injin (black rice pudding with coconut milk) from a street vendor or local café — IDR 20,000–30,000
meals.lunch: Pack a self-prepared picnic or buy from a roadside warung while cycling — budget IDR 30,000–40,000
meals.dinner: Beachside BBQ warung — grilled corn, satay, and tempeh with rice for IDR 50,000–70,000

day_by_day.notes: Ask resort staff for their personal recommendations for hidden beaches and authentic village experiences — locals always know the best spots tourists miss. Respect local customs during village visits.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike or coastal walk — wake before dawn for a 2–3 hour coastal hike along the clifftops or beach. Watch the sunrise paint the sky in pinks and oranges over the ocean. This is a free and deeply memorable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Treat yourself to a traditional Balinese spa treatment — a 2-hour package including a Lulur body scrub, floral bath, and Balinese massage at a local spa costs IDR 150,000–250,000. A perfect mid-trip indulgence that remains budget-friendly.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Legong or Barong dance performance at a local cultural center — tickets cost IDR 80,000–150,000. These traditional Balinese dances tell stories of gods, demons, and ancient legends through elaborate costumes and precise movements.

meals.breakfast: Post-hike energy boost — Jamu (traditional herbal tonic) and a banana pancake from a street stall for IDR 20,000–35,000
meals.lunch: Healthy warung lunch — Gado-Gado (steamed vegetables with peanut sauce) and fresh coconut water for IDR 35,000–50,000
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner near the cultural center — Nasi Campur with a selection of traditional sides for IDR 45,000–65,000

day_by_day.notes: For the sunrise hike, bring a torch/flashlight, water, and insect repellent. Book the spa treatment in advance as popular spots fill up. Cultural performances usually start at 19:00 or 19:30 — arrive 20 minutes early.

day_by_day.morning: Final yoga morning — attend a special 2-hour yoga workshop at your favorite studio from the trip. Choose a style you haven't tried yet — Aerial Yoga, AcroYoga, or a sound healing session (IDR 100,000–200,000). A meaningful way to deepen your practice before heading home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last beach afternoon — return to your favorite beach from the trip for a final swim. Collect your thoughts, take photos, and savor the warm Bali sun. Buy a few last-minute gifts or souvenirs from beach vendors (bargain kindly).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — slightly splurge on your final night. Choose a beachfront restaurant with a beautiful view for a memorable last meal. Toast to a wonderful trip.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory breakfast — full Indonesian breakfast with Nasi Goreng, fried egg, fresh fruit, and Bali coffee at a nice warung for IDR 50,000–70,000
meals.lunch: Light beach snack — fresh coconut, tropical fruit platter, and spring rolls from a beach vendor for IDR 30,000–45,000
meals.dinner: Farewell beachfront dinner — splurge slightly with a seafood platter, Bintang, and dessert for IDR 150,000–200,000

day_by_day.notes: Use the final afternoon to repack, settle any outstanding bills at the resort, and prepare for departure. Keep some IDR cash for tips — tipping is appreciated but not mandatory. Reflect on your journey and the experiences you've had.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise on the beach — wake early for one last sunrise meditation or yoga practice on the sand. Breathe in the ocean air and express gratitude for the trip. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort (standard checkout is 11:00 — confirm with reception).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — if time allows, visit a final local café for a leisurely lunch and last Bali coffee. Browse any remaining shops or markets near the resort. Head to Ngurah Rai International Airport (allow 1.5–2 hours travel time from beach areas).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Bali — carry the warmth, relaxation, and yoga practice home with you.

meals.breakfast: Final Bali breakfast — Bubur Ayam or banana pancakes at a beloved warung discovered during the trip for IDR 25,000–40,000
meals.lunch: Airport lunch or a final warung meal near the resort before departure — IDR 40,000–60,000
meals.dinner: Meal on the return flight or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport check-in — Bali airport can be busy. Arrive at least 2.5–3 hours before international flights. Declare any food items at customs. Keep a small amount of IDR for any last-minute airport purchases or tips. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Bali Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort, Bali (Beachfront). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely first walk along the beachfront to get oriented. Dip your toes in the warm Indian Ocean and relax on the resort's beach loungers.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to a nearby beachside warung (local eatery) for a relaxed welcome dinner. Watch the sunset from the beach and enjoy the warm Bali evening air.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at the airport or during transfer
meals.dinner: Seaside warung near the resort — try Nasi Goreng or Mie Goreng with fresh coconut water (~IDR 60,000–100,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Hydrate well after the flight. Exchange some currency to IDR at the airport for small local purchases. Confirm resort amenities and yoga schedule at check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Join the resort's morning yoga session on the beachfront deck at sunrise (approximately 06:30). Gentle Hatha or Vinyasa flow with ocean views — perfect for resetting after travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local beach area on foot or by rented bicycle. Visit a nearby temple close to the shoreline (such as a coastal pura/sea temple) and observe local offerings and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a mid-range beachfront restaurant for dinner. Enjoy fresh grilled fish or prawn satay with a Bintang beer or fresh juice while watching the stars over the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or local café — fresh tropical fruit platter, eggs, and Balinese coffee (~IDR 80,000–150,000)
meals.lunch: Beachside café — grilled corn, fresh coconut, and a light sandwich or salad (~IDR 70,000–120,000)
meals.dinner: Mid-range beachfront restaurant — grilled seafood platter with rice (~IDR 150,000–250,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Apply sunscreen generously. The July sun in Bali is warm even with only 30mm of rain expected this month. Bring a light sarong for temple visits.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga on the beach independently or with a local instructor. Follow with a swim in the calm morning sea. The water is warm and visibility is typically excellent in July.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a day trip to a famous surf beach nearby (e.g., Kuta, Seminyak, or Canggu depending on resort location). Take a beginner or intermediate surf lesson (~IDR 200,000–350,000 for 2 hours including board rental).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local night market (pasar malam) for authentic Balinese street food. Try Sate Lilit, Pisang Goreng, and fresh fruit juices.

meals.breakfast: Resort or local café — smoothie bowl with dragon fruit, banana, and granola (~IDR 80,000–130,000)
meals.lunch: Warung near the surf beach — Nasi Campur (mixed rice with sides) (~IDR 40,000–80,000)
meals.dinner: Night market street food — budget-friendly and authentic (~IDR 50,000–100,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Surf lessons are widely available and instructors are generally very accommodating for all levels. Book in advance or on the day at the beach. Wear reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach walk followed by a guided meditation or pranayama breathing session at the resort or a nearby yoga shala. Focus on mindfulness and setting intentions for the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local Balinese spa for a traditional Balinese massage and body scrub treatment (~IDR 200,000–350,000 for 90 minutes). This is a signature Bali experience and excellent mid-trip recovery.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the nearest town center. Try Bebek Betutu (slow-cooked duck) or Babi Guling (suckling pig) — iconic Balinese dishes.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Balinese porridge (bubur) or toast with local jam and tropical fruit (~IDR 80,000–150,000)
meals.lunch: Light warung lunch near the spa — Gado-Gado (peanut sauce salad) or Pecel (~IDR 40,000–70,000)
meals.dinner: Local Balinese restaurant in town — Bebek Betutu or Babi Guling set menu (~IDR 120,000–200,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book your spa treatment in advance as popular spots fill up quickly. Many spas offer package deals for multiple treatments at a discount.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning yoga class at a dedicated yoga studio (e.g., a well-reviewed shala nearby). Choose an intermediate Ashtanga or Yin Yoga class for a deeper practice (~IDR 100,000–180,000 per class).
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach afternoon — snorkeling session off the coast. Rent snorkel gear (~IDR 50,000–80,000) or join a guided snorkel tour (~IDR 250,000–400,000) to explore coral reefs and tropical fish.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at a beachfront bar followed by dinner. Enjoy the golden hour over the water with a fresh mocktail or Arak cocktail.

meals.breakfast: Pre-yoga light snack — banana and local black rice pudding (~IDR 30,000–60,000)
meals.lunch: Post-snorkel warung — fresh fish soup (Soto Ikan) with steamed rice (~IDR 60,000–100,000)
meals.dinner: Beachfront bar and grill — grilled barramundi or tuna steak with vegetables (~IDR 150,000–250,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check snorkel tour conditions with operators — July is generally excellent for underwater visibility in Bali. Bring an underwater camera or waterproof phone case.

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to Ubud — Bali's cultural heart (~1–2 hours by private driver, ~IDR 300,000–500,000 return). Morning visit to the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary and Ubud Royal Palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud Art Market for handmade crafts, batik textiles, and souvenirs. Stroll through Ubud's charming streets and visit a local art gallery or woodcarving workshop.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak Fire Dance performance at Uluwatu Temple or Ubud Palace at sunset (~IDR 100,000–150,000 per person). Dinner in Ubud before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast or grab-and-go — local rice cake (lontong) and tea (~IDR 40,000–80,000)
meals.lunch: Ubud mid-range café — organic salad, tempeh bowl, and fresh juice (~IDR 100,000–180,000)
meals.dinner: Ubud restaurant — Rijsttafel (Indonesian rice table feast) or traditional Balinese set menu (~IDR 150,000–250,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hire a trusted local driver for the Ubud day trip — negotiate a full-day rate (~IDR 500,000–700,000). Wear a sarong at temple sites. Monkey Forest tip: do not bring food or shiny objects.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Gentle beach yoga independently or resort class. Spend time journaling, reading, or simply relaxing in a hammock by the sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a quieter, less-touristy beach nearby — ask resort staff for recommendations for hidden coves or secluded stretches of coastline. Bring a book and enjoy the solitude.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or join a Balinese cooking class nearby (~IDR 250,000–400,000 per person). Learn to make signature dishes like Sate, Lawar, and Black Rice Pudding. Eat what you cook!

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full tropical spread with fresh papaya, pineapple, eggs, and Balinese coffee (~IDR 100,000–150,000)
meals.lunch: Beachside snack — corn on the cob, fresh coconut, and fruit (~IDR 30,000–60,000)
meals.dinner: Cooking class dinner — you prepare and eat your own Balinese feast (~IDR 250,000–400,000 includes meal)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important for a balanced itinerary. Cooking classes are a wonderful cultural experience and a great way to meet fellow travelers. Book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga at sunrise on the beach. Follow with a refreshing sea swim and a walk collecting shells along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby waterfall (e.g., Gitgit, Sekumpul, or a local waterfall depending on resort location). Hire a scooter (~IDR 70,000–100,000/day) or join a guided tour (~IDR 200,000–350,000).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a relaxing evening. Optional: sunset boat ride or traditional jukung (outrigger canoe) experience with a local fisherman (~IDR 150,000–250,000).

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga snack then full breakfast after — local bakery or café with pastries and fruit (~IDR 70,000–120,000)
meals.lunch: Warung near the waterfall — simple rice and vegetable dishes (~IDR 40,000–70,000)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or nearby mid-range spot — fresh pasta or Indonesian fusion (~IDR 120,000–200,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Waterfall trails can be slippery — wear appropriate footwear. Bring a change of clothes as you will likely get wet. July weather is ideal for waterfall visits with lower water volume and clearer paths.

day_by_day.morning: Intensive yoga workshop or two-hour class at a reputable local studio. Focus on alignment, breathwork, and deepening your practice. Many studios offer drop-in workshops (~IDR 150,000–250,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach volleyball or other water sports (paddleboarding, kayaking) available at the resort or nearby beach club (~IDR 100,000–200,000 per activity).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a slightly upscale mid-range restaurant for a treat. Try a modern Balinese or Indonesian fusion menu with creative cocktails or mocktails.

meals.breakfast: Pre-workshop fuel — banana pancakes (a Bali classic) with honey and coffee (~IDR 60,000–100,000)
meals.lunch: Post-yoga healthy café — acai bowl, avocado toast, or noodle salad (~IDR 90,000–160,000)
meals.dinner: Mid-range fusion restaurant — tasting menu or à la carte Indonesian fusion (~IDR 200,000–350,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Many yoga studios in Bali attract international teachers and offer unique workshops. Check community boards or Instagram for pop-up events during your stay.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hike or walk to a scenic viewpoint near the resort area. Bring water and a light jacket for the early morning breeze. Photograph the stunning Bali landscape at golden hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach day — set up a comfortable spot, read, swim, and enjoy the warm July weather. Treat yourself to a fresh coconut and tropical fruit from a beach vendor.
day_by_day.evening: Join a group beach bonfire or sunset gathering if available (check with resort). Alternatively, enjoy a quiet dinner for two at a romantic beachside table.

meals.breakfast: Early hike snack — energy bar and water, then post-hike breakfast at a local café (~IDR 80,000–130,000)
meals.lunch: Beach vendor or nearby warung — Martabak (stuffed pancake) or fresh fruit plate (~IDR 40,000–80,000)
meals.dinner: Romantic beachside restaurant — grilled lobster or fish with rice and salad (~IDR 200,000–350,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check with resort staff about the best local sunrise viewpoints. Some may require a short motorbike or car ride. Stay hydrated during the hike even in cooler morning temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Final deep-dive yoga session — consider a private one-on-one yoga class with a local teacher for personalized instruction (~IDR 200,000–350,000 for 90 minutes).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local village or cultural center to learn about Balinese Hindu traditions, offerings (canang sari), and daily spiritual rituals. Many villages welcome respectful visitors.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style dinner at the resort's restaurant or a highly-rated local spot. Celebrate the penultimate evening with a special meal and reflect on the journey.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread including local black rice porridge, tropical fruits, and Balinese coffee (~IDR 100,000–150,000)
meals.lunch: Village warung or local family restaurant — home-cooked Balinese food (~IDR 50,000–90,000)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or top-rated local restaurant — special set menu dinner (~IDR 250,000–400,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Private yoga sessions can be arranged through the resort or local yoga studios. Balinese village visits are best done with a local guide to ensure cultural sensitivity and proper etiquette.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach meditation and yoga practice. Take a long, mindful walk along the beach, collecting memories and final photographs of the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at local markets or art shops. Pick up Balinese crafts, essential oils, sarongs, or locally made jewelry. Bargain politely and enjoy the interaction.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at your favorite restaurant from the trip — revisit a place that made an impression. Toast to an incredible 13 days in Bali.

meals.breakfast: Favorite local café or resort — recreate your best breakfast from the trip (~IDR 80,000–150,000)
meals.lunch: Light warung lunch — keep it simple and local (~IDR 50,000–80,000)
meals.dinner: Return to a favorite restaurant — order your top dishes from the trip as a farewell meal (~IDR 150,000–300,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pack non-essentials tonight to make departure day smoother. Keep one outfit and essentials accessible for Day 13 morning. Confirm checkout time with the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning gentle yoga or beach walk for the last time. Breathe in the ocean air and practice gratitude for the trip. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Bali Ngurah Rai International Airport. Allow at least 2–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Browse duty-free for last Balinese treats (Kopi Luwak coffee, local chocolate, Balinese spice kits).
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry warm memories, a recharged spirit, and a deeper yoga practice back home.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast or nearby café — go out with a classic Balinese breakfast (~IDR 80,000–130,000)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café — keep it light before the flight (~IDR 100,000–180,000 at airport prices)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Bali airport can be busy — arrive with plenty of time. Double-check baggage weight as souvenirs add up. Confirm no restricted items (fresh fruits, certain foods) in your luggage for customs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Bali's Ngurah Rai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a traditional Balinese welcome ceremony with flower garlands and refreshing coconut water. Check in to your beachfront suite, unpack, and take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to soak in the warm afternoon sun (avg. 25°C).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's infinity pool bar overlooking the Indian Ocean. Gentle introduction to the resort's amenities with a guided tour by your personal concierge.

meals.breakfast: Enjoyed on the flight or at the airport lounge.
meals.lunch: Welcome light bites and tropical fruit platter served upon check-in at the resort.
meals.dinner: Romantic beachfront dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant — fresh Jimbaran-style grilled seafood platter with Balinese spices, paired with a curated selection of white wines.

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in in advance if possible. Tip your transfer driver and resort staff generously. Keep the first evening relaxed to recover from jet lag.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the private beach led by the resort's expert yoga instructor. Practice pranayama and gentle asanas as the sun rises over the ocean horizon — a deeply restorative start to your Bali journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling excursion along the nearby coral reef, arranged by the resort's water sports concierge. Explore vibrant marine life in crystal-clear warm waters, followed by a relaxing session on a sun lounger with chilled towels and tropical juice service.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak fire dance performance at a nearby clifftop temple (private transport arranged by the resort). Return for a candlelit dinner on your suite's private terrace.

meals.breakfast: Lavish à la carte breakfast at the resort's ocean-view restaurant — freshly baked pastries, tropical fruit bowls, eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, and cold-pressed juices.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — grilled tiger prawns, avocado salad, and coconut-lime dressing with sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner — Balinese duck confit (bebek betutu) with steamed jasmine rice, sautéed morning glory, and a bottle of chilled Sauvignon Blanc.

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen for the snorkeling excursion. Wear a light sarong for the temple visit in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Vinyasa flow yoga class at the resort's open-air yoga pavilion surrounded by tropical gardens. Follow with a 60-minute Balinese massage at the resort's luxury spa to release travel tension.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the nearby Tanah Lot sea temple — one of Bali's most iconic landmarks perched on a rocky outcrop. Explore the surrounding cliffs and take in dramatic coastal views. Browse artisan stalls for premium Balinese crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour at a clifftop luxury beach club near Tanah Lot, then return to the resort for a relaxed evening by the pool.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast — fresh tropical fruit platter, Greek yogurt with local honey, Nasi Goreng (Balinese fried rice), and freshly brewed Balinese coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant near Tanah Lot — grilled mahi-mahi with sambal matah, steamed rice, and fresh coconut water.
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant dinner — slow-braised wagyu beef short rib with Balinese black pepper sauce, roasted root vegetables, and a glass of Malbec.

day_by_day.notes: Tanah Lot is best visited in the late afternoon for golden-hour photography. Wear comfortable walking sandals.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga and meditation session on the beach, followed by a guided breathwork (pranayama) class with the resort's senior yoga therapist. Enjoy a post-session herbal tea ceremony in the garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area with a private guided walk through a nearby fishing village. Interact with local fishermen, observe traditional boat-making, and visit a local coconut sugar producer for a hands-on tasting experience.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury sunset sailing cruise aboard a private catamaran — enjoy chilled champagne, canapés, and panoramic views of Bali's coastline as the sun dips below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — international and Balinese stations featuring made-to-order omelets, smoked salmon, artisan cheeses, and fresh-pressed juices.
meals.lunch: Beachside warung lunch (premium local eatery) — Babi Guling (suckling pig) rice box, fresh cucumber salad, and iced lemongrass tea.
meals.dinner: Canapés and light bites served on the sunset sailing cruise — charcuterie boards, fresh oysters, bruschetta, and champagne.

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset sailing cruise at least two days in advance through the resort concierge. Bring a light layer for the sea breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Restorative Yin Yoga session at the resort's beachside pavilion, followed by a 90-minute hot stone massage at the spa. Take time to float in the resort's private plunge pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Seminyak — Bali's upscale shopping and lifestyle district. Browse luxury boutiques, designer surf brands, and high-end art galleries. Visit Ku De Ta or Potato Head Beach Club for a premium afternoon experience.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Seminyak's top fine-dining restaurants, then private transfer back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast — shakshuka with artisan sourdough, fresh tropical fruit, Balinese single-origin espresso, and a green detox juice.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Seminyak café — lobster bisque, grilled barramundi fillet with herb butter, and a glass of chilled Chablis.
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Seminyak — 5-course tasting menu featuring modern Indonesian cuisine with wine pairings at a top-rated restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Seminyak is approximately 30–45 minutes from most beachfront resort areas — arrange private return transport in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-morning yoga immersion — a 2-hour Ashtanga yoga masterclass at the resort followed by a guided sound healing session using Tibetan singing bowls and crystal bowls in the garden pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private surf lesson with a certified instructor on one of Bali's renowned beginner-friendly surf breaks. Equipment, rash guard, and refreshments are included.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort — soak in your suite's private outdoor bathtub filled with frangipani flowers, then enjoy a nightcap at the resort's rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Healthy resort breakfast — acai bowl with granola and local honey, poached eggs on avocado toast, fresh papaya, and cold-brew coffee.
meals.lunch: Post-surf beachside lunch — grilled corn-fed chicken with chimichurri, sweet potato fries, fresh watermelon juice.
meals.dinner: Resort rooftop restaurant dinner — pan-seared sea bass with lemongrass beurre blanc, jasmine rice, and steamed bok choy, paired with a crisp Pinot Grigio.

day_by_day.notes: Surf lessons are suitable for all levels. Apply reef-safe SPF 50+ sunscreen before entering the water.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach walk followed by a private Balinese cooking class — learn to prepare traditional dishes such as sate lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding using fresh local ingredients from the morning market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxation afternoon at the resort — enjoy the spa's hydrotherapy circuit (steam room, cold plunge pool, Jacuzzi), followed by a 60-minute aromatherapy facial.
day_by_day.evening: Special Balinese ceremonial dinner experience on the beach — dine on the dishes prepared in your morning cooking class, accompanied by a traditional gamelan music performance.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-class breakfast — seasonal fruit plate, yogurt parfait, and Balinese ginger tea.
meals.lunch: Tasting lunch of the dishes prepared during your morning cooking class — sate lilit, lawar salad, and black rice pudding for dessert.
meals.dinner: Ceremonial beachfront dinner — traditional Balinese feast with live gamelan music, tropical fruit dessert platter, and Arak cocktails.

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically begins at 8:00 AM with a market visit — confirm timing with the concierge. A perfect midpoint celebration of your trip.

day_by_day.morning: Morning meditation and breathwork session on the beach at sunrise. Follow with a long, leisurely swim in the resort's infinity pool, then read or journal on your private terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided snorkeling or scuba diving excursion to a nearby dive site — explore underwater temples, vibrant coral gardens, and tropical fish. Certified PADI guides available.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beach bar, followed by a stargazing experience on the beach with a telescope provided by the resort concierge.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — eggs any style, smoked salmon platter, fresh croissants, tropical fruit bowl, and freshly squeezed orange juice.
meals.lunch: On-boat packed premium lunch during the diving excursion — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, energy bars, and chilled water.
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant dinner — whole grilled lobster with garlic herb butter, saffron rice, grilled asparagus, and a bottle of premier Chardonnay.

day_by_day.notes: Non-divers can opt for snorkeling. Bring an underwater camera or rent a GoPro from the resort's water sports desk.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle morning yoga flow on the beach, then embark on a full-day excursion to Ubud — Bali's cultural and spiritual heartland. Private luxury vehicle with a knowledgeable guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud's highlights — visit the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary, browse the Ubud Art Market for premium batik and silverwork, and tour the Ubud Royal Palace. Stop at a renowned local gallery to view traditional and contemporary Balinese art.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Ubud's world-class fine-dining restaurants set amid rice terraces, then private transfer back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast before departure — granola with coconut milk, fresh tropical fruits, avocado toast, and cold-brew coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Ubud restaurant — organic farm-to-table menu featuring local vegetables, tempeh, and Balinese herb-crusted chicken with rice.
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Ubud — modern Balinese tasting menu with paired cocktails featuring local spirits, enjoyed overlooking illuminated rice terraces.

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is approximately 1.5 hours from the coast — depart by 9:00 AM for a full day. Wear comfortable shoes for walking the Monkey Forest trails.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Kundalini yoga and chakra-balancing meditation session at the resort's garden pavilion. Follow with a luxurious 2-hour couples' spa journey — body scrub, wrap, and deep tissue massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private beach time — set up a luxury cabana on the resort's private beach with personal butler service, chilled beverages, and fresh fruit platters. Enjoy stand-up paddleboarding or kayaking.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-suite romantic dinner — a chef comes to your suite to prepare a bespoke 4-course Balinese-inspired menu. Candlelight, flower petals, and a curated wine list included.

meals.breakfast: Resort restaurant breakfast — smoked salmon eggs Benedict, fresh-pressed green juice, tropical fruit platter, and Balinese single-origin pour-over coffee.
meals.lunch: Butler-served beach lunch — chilled prawn cocktail, lobster salad wrap, sparkling water, and a selection of premium iced teas.
meals.dinner: Private in-suite chef's dinner — amuse-bouche, seared tuna tataki, slow-roasted lamb rack with Balinese spice crust, and a passion fruit soufflé for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Book the in-suite private chef experience at least 48 hours in advance. This is an ideal day for couples seeking total relaxation and privacy.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided hike to a nearby coastal viewpoint or sacred spring — witness panoramic views of the coastline and lush tropical jungle at golden hour. Return for a refreshing outdoor shower and light breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a premium Balinese spa village for a traditional Mandi Lulur ritual — a centuries-old royal Javanese treatment involving herbal scrubs, turmeric masks, and floral milk baths. A deeply immersive cultural wellness experience.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the resort's infinity pool bar. Enjoy a leisurely final dinner at the resort's top restaurant with the ocean as your backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Post-hike resort breakfast — protein-rich options including smoked salmon, poached eggs, grain bowls, fresh tropical juices, and Balinese coffee.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the spa village — organic salad bowls, fresh spring rolls, and herbal wellness teas.
meals.dinner: Premium resort dinner — Balinese-spiced rack of lamb, truffle mashed potatoes, seasonal vegetables, and a decadent chocolate lava cake with vanilla bean ice cream, paired with a fine red wine.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes for the morning walk. The Mandi Lulur ritual is approximately 2.5–3 hours — book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise yoga session on the beach — a reflective, meditative practice to honor your Bali journey. Followed by journaling and herbal tea on your private terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping — visit a curated selection of premium Balinese boutiques for high-quality souvenirs: hand-painted silk scarves, sterling silver jewelry, premium Balinese coffee, and artisan ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset farewell dinner at a cliffside luxury restaurant with sweeping ocean panoramas — the perfect way to bid farewell to Bali.

meals.breakfast: Grand resort breakfast — full spread of international and local dishes, freshly baked pastries, tropical fruits, and premium coffee.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a beachside café — grilled barramundi tacos, fresh guacamole, and chilled coconut water.
meals.dinner: Cliffside farewell dinner — 6-course degustation menu with Balinese and French influences, premium wine pairings, and a personalized dessert platter.

day_by_day.notes: Reserve the cliffside restaurant at least 3 days in advance as it is highly popular. Request a window table for the best sunset views.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle final morning — enjoy a slow breakfast on your private terrace, take a last dip in the infinity pool, and soak in the final views of the Indian Ocean. Begin packing and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort with a warm farewell from the resort team. Private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Arrive with ample time before your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali with cherished memories, a deeply rested body, and a renewed spirit. Enjoy the airport's premium lounge facilities before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final in-suite or terrace breakfast — fresh tropical fruits, yogurt, croissants, and Balinese coffee to savor one last time.
meals.lunch: Light pre-flight lunch at the airport's premium lounge or a farewell meal at an airport restaurant — nasi goreng, fresh spring rolls, and iced lemongrass tea.
meals.dinner: Dinner on board or at your next destination.

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout (subject to availability) to maximize your final morning. Confirm airport transfer timing with the concierge the evening before. Keep a small bag of Balinese snacks and coffee for the journey home.
